papers.title: 3D Bioprinting Human Chondrocytes with Nanocellulose–Alginate Bioink for Cartilage Tissue Engineering Applications
papers.abstract: The introduction of 3D bioprinting is expected to revolutionize the field of tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. The 3D bioprinter is able to dispense materials while moving in X, Y, and Z directions, which enables the engineering of complex structures from the bottom up. In this study, a bioink that combines the outstanding shear thinning properties of nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC) with the fast cross-linking ability of alginate was formulated for the 3D bioprinting of living soft tissue with cells. Printability was evaluated with concern to printer parameters and shape fidelity. The shear thinning behavior of the tested bioinks enabled printing of both 2D gridlike structures as well as 3D constructs. Furthermore, anatomically shaped cartilage structures, such as a human ear and sheep meniscus, were 3D printed using MRI and CT images as blueprints. Human chondrocytes bioprinted in the noncytotoxic, nanocellulose-based bioink exhibited a cell viability of 73% and 86% after 1 and 7 days of 3D culture, respectively. On the basis of these results, we can conclude that the nanocellulose-based bioink is a suitable hydrogel for 3D bioprinting with living cells. This study demonstrates the potential use of nanocellulose for 3D bioprinting of living tissues and organs.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及生物打印软骨组织，但未使用AI技术，与AI生物打印方向不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage; it focuses solely on bioink formulation and cell viability.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发适合软骨组织工程的生物墨水
summary_zh.method: 将纳米纤维素与海藻酸盐混合，3D打印软骨细胞
summary_zh.result: 细胞存活率在7天后达86%，可打印耳廓等结构
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞培养验证生物相容性

summary_en.motivation: To formulate a bioink with suitable rheological properties for 3D bioprinting of living cartilage tissue.
summary_en.method: Nanofibrillated cellulose and alginate were combined to create a shear-thinning bioink for extrusion-based bioprinting of human chondrocytes.
summary_en.result: The bioink supported cell viability of 73% and 86% after 1 and 7 days, and enabled printing of anatomically shaped constructs like a human ear.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and viability assays were performed on printed constructs.

papers.title: Clinical marginal and internal fit of metal ceramic crowns fabricated with a selective laser melting technology
papers.first_author_affiliation: Resident, Department of Prosthodontics, 9th People's Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai Key Laboratory of Stomatology, Shanghai, P.R. China

corresponding_authors.name: Xiuyin Zhang
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Professor, Department of Prosthodontics, 9th People's Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai Key Laboratory of Stomatology, Shanghai, P.R. China. Electronic address: xiuyinzhangxyz@163.com

llm.relevance_to_user: 与用户方向无关，关注牙科修复体边缘适合性，而非骨科植入物的应力遮挡或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures for stress shielding, LPBF fabrication with mechanical testing, fatigue behavior, or osseointegration; it is limited to dental crown fit evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估SLM制作金属烤瓷冠的边缘和内部适合性。
summary_zh.method: 使用SLM技术制作金属基底冠，测量边缘间隙和内部间隙。
summary_zh.result: SLM冠的边缘和内部间隙在临床可接受范围内，但粘接后间隙增大。
summary_zh.validation: 体外测量冠间隙并与传统铸造冠比较。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the clinical marginal and internal fit of metal-ceramic crowns fabricated using selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Metal copings were fabricated by SLM, and marginal and internal gaps were measured using silicone replica technique.
summary_en.result: SLM crowns showed clinically acceptable gaps, although cementation increased the internal gap.
summary_en.validation: In vitro measurement of crown gaps compared with conventionally cast crowns.
